answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network maps each agent identity to a graph vertex whose admission requires cryptographic stake burning. As an attacker expands forged identities, total burn requirements follow superlinear cost scaling: each new identity pushes staking depth over an exponential economic ledge, requiring miners to commit unrecoverable deposits as brittle as fractured shale. Attacker replication cost scales superlinearly as O(N^2).
